A_target.statement:
Let $\CC$ be the [[Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)|ring]] of [[Definition:Rational Cauchy Sequence|rational Cauchy sequences]] and $\NN$ the set of [[Definition:Null Sequence|null sequences]].
Then:
:$\R = \CC / \NN$
is a [[Definition:Complete Ordered Field|complete ordered field]] containing $\Q$.

B_source.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]] and $M$ a [[Definition:Maximal Ideal of Ring|maximal ideal]].
Then $R / M$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].

substitutions.the ring R: the ring of rational Cauchy sequences under pointwise operations
substitutions.the maximal ideal M: the ideal of sequences converging to zero

derived.invertibility of nonzero classes: the fact that a non-null Cauchy sequence is eventually bounded away from zero

validity_conditions: Cauchy sequences must be closed under pointwise product, which uses boundedness of Cauchy sequences
the null sequences must form an ideal, not merely a subgroup, for the quotient to be a ring
maximality of the null ideal must be checked directly, and is what makes the quotient a field rather than just a ring
proof_plan:
Form $\CC$ under pointwise addition and multiplication.
Sums and products of Cauchy sequences are Cauchy, as Cauchy sequences are bounded.

$\NN$ is closed under addition, and a bounded sequence times a null sequence is null.
Hence $\NN$ is an [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]].

Let $\sequence {a_n} \notin \NN$.
Then $\size {a_n} \ge \delta > 0$ for all $n \ge N$, and $b_n = a_n^{-1}$ for $n \ge N$ is Cauchy with $a_n b_n - 1$ eventually $0$.
Hence $\sequence {a_n}$ is invertible modulo $\NN$, and $\NN$ is [[Definition:Maximal Ideal of Ring|maximal]].
By [[Maximal Ideal iff Quotient Ring is Field]], $\CC / \NN$ is a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].

Embed $\Q$ via constant sequences.
Declare $\eqclass {a_n} {} > 0$ if $a_n \ge \delta > 0$ eventually; this gives an [[Definition:Ordered Field|ordered field]].
A diagonal argument shows every Cauchy sequence in $\CC / \NN$ converges, so the field is [[Definition:Complete Metric Space|complete]].
{{qed}}
